caption: N=1 baseline: a lever on the back of a sticky piston.

Pushes a block out two cells from a one-block-wide wall: the lever's piston shoves a strip of three slime blocks forward, and a second sticky piston riding on that strip pushes the block one step further; switching off pulls the strip back and the riding piston grabs the block home. How it works: an observer hanging under the strip blinks 2 ticks after every move and fires the riding piston (the lever's piston ignores it, a piston is never powered through its own face); the riding piston's short pulse leaves the block on the strip's front slime, which carries it back on the way home.
N=2, slime + observer, 7 blocks: the observer beside S1 powers it (B stands on it).

Pushes a block out two cells with no slime: two sticky pistons in a line; flipping the lever makes the back piston throw the front piston and the block forward, then the lever holds the front piston out; switching off brings them back one at a time. How it works: an observer next to the lever blinks on every flip and pulses the back piston (through the stone beside it); on the way back the front piston lets go, the back piston grabs it home, and a second observer carried along fires as it lands, so the front piston reaches out and grabs the block home.

N=2, slime-free, 7 blocks: an observer watching the input gives a 2 gt pulse on BOTH edges to A (through the stone beside it) and to a second sticky piston that carries an observer. On: A pushes B + payload and spits them (B lands next to the input, which holds it extended: the payload goes one more cell). Off: B retracts (payload back one), A's pulse reach-pulls B home, and the carried observer, pulled home too, fires on landing into B (variant 2: where it sits), whose 2 gt pulse reach-pulls the payload home. The lever hangs on the input observer.

How it works: two sticky pistons stacked under the sand; an observer under the lever blinks on every flip and pulses the bottom piston, which throws the top piston and the sand up one cell, and the lever holds the top piston up (sand one more cell); switching off, the top piston drops back, the sand falls onto it, and the bottom piston grabs the top one back down with the sand riding home.

The minimizer replaced observer runs of the timing chain by pistons used as delays.

Pulsers sit diagonal to the slime cells so no slime ever drags them.

Pushes a block out three cells from a one-block-wide wall, 16 blocks: a line of three sticky pistons with a slime block between each pair; each piston fires itself whenever it is moved (an observer rides on the slime behind it), and the observers above the line, run by a chain from the lever, start each wave of pushes (out) or grabs (back). How it works: going out, the middle piston pushes the front piston and the block, the front piston pushes the block on, then the back piston starts a second wave (back, middle, front); coming back the waves are front; middle, front; back, middle, front, each piston grabbing what the one in front left behind. The back and middle waves start with observers two above the line that power their piston through the cell above it. The front piston's observer rides ON TOP of its slime, facing up: when the lever goes off, the sticky piston under the lever pulls back right above it, the riding observer sees it and fires, and the front piston starts the way back with no starter of its own. The lever hangs on the side of the chain's first observer. Found by `mctas circuit pext lns --free-lever` (remove 3 blocks, the lever included, grow 2 back: 19 -> 18 -> 17 -> 16); game: robust (16 builds), redsim agrees.

How it works: the cascade train (going out the pistons push in waves; coming back the waves start front first and each piston grabs what the one in front left behind), every wave started by an observer two above the line that powers its piston through the empty cell above it. One unit's observer rides on top of its slime and doubles as a starter, the lever hangs on the side of the chain's first observer, and pistons in the chain stand in for chain observers (each lever flip moves a head the next observer sees). Found by `mctas circuit pext lns --free-lever --repeat` from the 26-block cascade (26 -> 25 -> 24 -> 23, faster at each step); game: robust (16 builds), redsim agrees.
